svg.text: CORRECT vs INCORRECT breadboard wiring (side by side) - one flex sensor, rows 21-31
WRONG 1: both tabs in the SAME row
Both tabs sit in row 25 (holes f25 and g25 are joined inside the board).
The two tabs are shorted together, so the sensor is bypassed and
its tab never reaches the node row 26. The node only has the 10 k
resistor to GND, so the ADC reads about 0 and does not react to bending.
FIX: tab 1 in row 25, tab 2 in row 26 (different rows). Red = shorted strip.
WRONG 2: row not connected to 3.3 V
The red jumper from row 25 to the 3.3 V rail is missing (or is in a rail
half that is not connected). The sensor gets no supply, the node
is pulled to GND by the 10 k, and the ADC reads about 0.
This matches the earlier prototype fault (ADC about 0-150).
FIX: jumper j25 to the 3.3 V rail; measure 3.3 V on row 25 (grey).
CORRECT: separate rows, resistor to GND
Tab 1 in row 25 (3.3 V via the red jumper). Tab 2 in row 26 (node).
The 10 k resistor goes from the node row 26 to row 29; a black jumper
joins row 29 to the GND rail. The green jumper takes the node to the
ESP32 ADC pin. Nothing else touches the node.
Pink = 3.3 V row, green = node row, grey = GND row (3 different strips).
